newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian debt/GDP ratio to fall further - Maystadt.
newsitem.headline: Belgian debt/GDP ratio to fall further - Maystadt.

text.p: Belgian Finance Minister Philippe Maystad said on Monday the ratio of state debt to gross domestic product should fall by six to 10 percentage points between 1998 and 2000.
He was speaking to European Union finance ministers on Belgium's updated convergence plan for economic and monetary union (EMU) in Europe.
"It will be a structural reduction which will draw exclusively on a reduction of the (budget) deficit," he said.

He said that between 1993 and 1997 the expected fall in the debt ratio would amount to 10 percentage points. Excluding one-off financial operations (capital gains on gold sales, a consolidation of public sector financial assets and revenue from privatisations) the contraction was five percentage points.
Maystadt noted that once the process of debt reduction had been started, it had developed a tendency to 'snowball'.

"A structural reduction by five points in four years compared with six to 10 points in the three following years -- that is a spontaneous acceleration of debt reduction following the stabilisation of the primary surplus," he said.
In December Maystadt said the debt/GDP ratio would fall to 127.0 percent in 1997 from 130.4 in 1996. By the year 2000 the ratio would be at 120.5 percent.
The Maastricht Treaty on EMU sets a goal of 60 percent for the debt/GDP ratio and states that higher ratios might be allowed provided there is a decline at a satisfactory pace.
At the time Maystadt said the primary budget surplus -- the difference between revenue and spending excluding debt financing costs -- would rise to 6.1 percent in 2000 from 5.4 percent in 1996.
